reviews.title: This app is AMAZING!
reviews.text:
JTL;DR:
If you are addicted to your phone, iPad, laptop, want to take back control of your life and actually live it as opposed to watching other people live theirs, or are setting it up for a children’s device, then Jomo is the app for you. It’s free to try and the free version is great too!                                                If I could give this 6 stars I would I mean this thing works amazingly AND IT’S SO CUSTOMIZABLE!! This gives your iPhone, MacBook, iPad, rail guards. Has probably saved me 100 hours of sleep by blocking the engineered addictive apps like YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok. And it’s extremely affordable too! Especially when compared with other similar apps. I’m incredibly happy with this product and their support (I had trouble setting up an automation) is incredibly quick to respond (I forgot to update the app). I love that!! I have probably 5 blocks on. One blocks all the addictive apps until I spend 5 minutes reading my Bible on the Bible app. Then another block only allows me to get up to 15 minutes of the app each time (I only allow myself 10 unblocks and the wait between unlock goes up each time (I find it gives me time to think if I really want to do this)). I only get unlimited time on those apps if I read my Bible for 25 minutes :). Adult content is always blocked (and blocked well!). I also have it set up to block the message app when a certain focus mode is on (so I can fully immerse myself in the work). Jomo app takes the decision of “should I put the phone down or one more video?” out of the equation and forces you to put down the phone (which is when you realize that you should’ve put it down long ago). I haven’t tried any of the other apps but from what I hear they cost way more and don’t even give you the same functionality/customizability. I have never had a reason to try another service. 
In terms of resource usage on the Mac, it’s very light (40-100 MB of RAM) which is always nice to have. I’m waiting for them to release a windows 10 version of Jomo, until then it’s Cold Turkey blocker.
I’ve been telling this to everyone I know (unfortunately a lot of them rather fight against the apps designed to make you addicted everyday). Oh and the free version is great too!! I think I upgraded to paid to get more than 3 blocks or something and also support the great work they’re doing. They have NO ADS (on either version), it’s extremely slick and well designed. Literally every Apple device I have has Jomo installed (besides Apple Watch but I don’t think they make Jomo for Apple Watch). 
Jomo team, if you’re reading this, thank you!! Please don’t sell out to private equity and make the app terrible.

reviews.title: Strong blocking, but missing real accountability
reviews.text:
This app does a good job enforcing Screen Time limits, but it falls short as an accountability tool.

Like most Screen Time apps, it relies on three mechanisms:
	•	app time limits
	•	unlocks / temporary access
	•	scheduled blocks

The problem is that following or breaking these rules isn’t meaningfully tracked. Users can:
	•	repeatedly use unlocks
	•	change limits or schedules after enforcement starts
	•	revoke Screen Time permissions and re-enable later

…without any persistent history or consequence inside the app. That makes it easy to undermine your own rules quietly, which defeats the purpose for serious users.

What would make this a 5-star app:
	•	an accountability history (unlock usage, schedule adherence, rule changes)
	•	logging Screen Time permission revocations/restores
	•	an integrity metric (did I keep my word or not)
	•	brief, optional reflection prompts at key moments (before unlocks, after rule changes)
	•	weekly summaries focused on accountability, not just usage minutes
	•	a place to define and revisit why you’re limiting apps, so behavior change is internal, not just enforced

Blocking alone changes behavior temporarily.
Accountability, integrity tracking, and reflection change it long-term.

If these additions were made, this would easily be a 5-star app.

 - Bugsnag (crash reports, which can be anonymized but Jomo is not)

 - Sendgrid (provides important email functions while also collecting massive amounts of customer data which has been leaked this year)

reviews.title: Wanted to love this app
reviews.text:
Honestly, I really wanted to love this app, but with all the issues on iOS, it’s just not worth it.

I understand that some limitations are on Apple’s side and not the developer’s fault. But even so, there are some things that don’t fully make sense, and despite trying to work with the FAQ and the support team, it seems like many of the problems won’t be fixable until iOS changes.

I really think screen time apps need to be more upfront about these limitations. A lot of features either don’t work as intended or require weird workarounds that defeat the purpose.

For example, in order to get accurate screen time data, I can only have Screen Time enabled on one of my devices. That makes the app’s shared feature kind of useless, since I have to turn off Screen Time on everything else.

Some parts of the UI get blocked properly, but others don’t—and that’s where I’m not sure if it’s an iOS issue or not. Like, user authentication screens get blocked, but game overlays don’t? The suggestion from support was to “exclude” those apps, but they don’t even show up in the exclusion list—so again, the feature just doesn’t work.

And there’s also the issue with using other focus tools. I can’t even use the Forest app, which is super basic, because the two interfere with each other. (For what it’s worth, Forest doesn’t interfere with Jomo.)

I’m sure this app works fine for people who just want to block specific apps—but if everything else is breaking or unreliable, it’s hard to justify paying for something that ends up increasing your screen time just because you’re constantly troubleshooting it. You might as well just use the built-in Screen Time settings on your phone. Maybe I will be trying this app again and updating this review when the new iOS drop. Till then I will stick with the settings on my phone.

reviews.title: The best screen time control app out there!
reviews.text:
Jomo is absolutely the best screen time blocking app, and I’ll tell you why. I came from an app named like a gem (starting with the letter O) that worked pretty well, but left much to be desired. -Really tough blocking. “Other” apps are too simple to disable blocks/rules that you set. Jomo has some hardcore features that really make it tough to break through
-Highly customizable configurations. With a Plus account, you can really customize block times, amounts, unlocks, etc. It’s very detailed and allows you to set it how you like
-Super reasonable price! “Other” apps charged a CRAZY amount; Jomo has super reasonable pricing, especially with the annual subscription, or even the lifetime pass
-Responsive support! The team was super responsive to some questions I had, and it’s clear they really care about building and maintaining this app

Shout out to Jomo and the team behind it; they really thought of everything. I’m really excited to get it dialed in, and can’t wait to see what the future of this app brings!

reviews.title: Actually SO helpful!!!
reviews.text:
I recently transitioned into a phase where I can work at my own pace, and I quickly realized that I struggle with self-control when I'm on my laptop. *Enter Jomo stage left*. I’ve tried many screen management tools, but Jomo is by far the easiest to use. It works on both apps and websites (I’m looking at you, Facebook!).

One of the features I appreciate the most is the tips and tricks it offers when I attempt to access a blocked site or app. They make me pause and reconsider why I even clicked in the first place, which has made me more intentional about my choices. Another great feature is the "break timer" delay. The five-second pause before starting the break often helps me realize I don’t really need to disrupt my workflow just because something challenging came up and it’s easier to scroll than to deal with it.

Overall, it’s the little things—along with the bigger features—that have made a difference. Not only has Jomo helped me manage my time more effectively, but it's also improved my self-discipline in a way that I hadn't expected.

I’m upset I didn’t find Jomo sooner! I’ve tried everything to stop doomscrolling and take back my time—Brick, Opal, grayscale screens, deleting apps—you name it. It finally clicked for me: we live in a time where your attention is money. If you’re mindlessly giving away your attention, you’re just a monkey scrolling, feeding into this dopamine trap.

Before you complain, “Oh, it’s $30 a year,” just think: that’s like two drinks at a bar. If you’re competitive like me, you’ll love the leaderboards where you can compete with friends and hold each other accountable. It’s fun, and we even have a group chat to stay on top of each other! Seriously, thank you to the Jomo team for creating something that actually helps fight against the endless scrolling. I can’t wait to see this app take off—it’s the only one I truly believe can beat brain rot.

I started with a hard lock out, and now I have enough self control that a 70-character random string is enough to keep me out except for “emergencies”. It took my brain not being drenched in Reddit and TikTok and YouTube to see that they’re actually more enjoyable in small doses. It won’t fix your life alone, but it is an incredible tool. I’ve communicated with both Laureline and Thomas about different things and they were  responsive and helpful. reviews.title: Best I’ve tried - tons of customization
reviews.text:

But you can go all in with rules, like I need to have meditated for 8 minutes to unlock any of my social media apps. The blocks can have a certain number of breaks and you can set the max time limit for the break. You can set the delay before taking a break. reviews.title: It’s good but maybe I’m not using it properly
reviews.text:
I’m enjoying the app. I love that it dims distracting apps on my phone so I know I can’t access them. Couple things I’ve noted in my use:

• Not sure if there was a proper walkthrough of each restriction option when I got the free trial, but I found I stuck to “Conscious Break” because that’s the first one I tried and didn’t know how the others worked. A pop up walkthrough would definitely encourage me to use more features

• I wish I could personalize the timer on how long I have to wait to take a conscious break. So, it starts at 5-6 seconds, but I need that to be at least 15 in order for me to give up and go back to my task (for a truly conscious break). Worried it created a bad habit where I just set my phone down and wait for the longer countdowns and take an unconscious break because the 5-6 second unlock time was too easy to get through

• I’m really not sure if there’s anything you can do about this one 😆 but when using the intention unlock feature, I’ve just typed a random letter to unlock it. Sometimes I use it properly—that helps my ADHD brain stay focused for sure. But I definitely get around it too quickly for it to be a truly conscious break

• It’d be great if the notifications of “time to get back to focusing” didn’t happen 30 seconds before the app closes. I wish it’d be more like 2 minutes before so I can save a video for later or wind down from my feed. I get frustrated and always fear losing the post when it kicks me out way too quickly.

I only tried the free version of Opal, but that was a little too hard to get into apps, and I think I rebelled a bit by the end and didn’t want to restrict myself at all. I like the flexibility of Jomo instead.  

Overall, I’m not sure if I like this app or Opal Better. I think price is much better here. If you guys gamify Jomo the way Opal does (theirs is a bit overkill though) and tighten up some features, you’d have an incredible product.

All that being said, it’s definitely helped me focus. Keep up the good work.

reviews.title: Superbly Crafted & The Free Option Is Surprisingly Feature Rich
reviews.text:
This review focuses only on the Free Tier (not the free trial option for Pro, which is separate). 

Tl;dr: The free option is so good it’s convinced me that the even more feature rich Pro option is absolutely going to be worth my money. I’m a big believer in supporting devs who clearly put in a ton of care and attention to their apps. 

-Free Tier can be used as many times as you need. Absolutely shocking considering the amount of features you get just with the free option.

-No ads. The devs really do believe their product is good enough to convince you that it’s worth the money. I absolutely agree with them. 

-Better stats than the the default App Limit feature on iOS : Offers you a lot more insights into those activities. You can even sort apps by activity types (i.e procrastination from doom-scrolling vs using apps for studying, you can create custom activity types too). You can even get trendlines on how much better you are at keeping goals and staying out of apps that distract overtime. 

-Great design philosophy: the UI is absolutely fantastic and very coherent. Nothing is jarring. Besides UI, I love how when you first start the app it asks you what types of goals you have using the app and what you intend to use the app for. Excellent. A good amount of premade scheduling templates. 

-Granular even when free: It goes beyond what App Limit does and gives you 3 different ways to do it. 

1. Set a blocking session: You can set what apps to block, how long you need them blocked in a day (during certain times or all day), what days in the week you need them blocked for. You can also enable and disable breaks, and control the amount of time a break is. You can also set it that when you take a break you have to then explain what the break is for if you need it to keep you accountable.

2. App Limit Conditionals: Works like App Limit but with the added benefit that you can tell it what times the app limit kicks in and when. 

3. Activity Conditionals: You can ask it to block apps until a you complete a certain goal, like exercise or studying a certain amount of things. Also can choose when this happen just like the two modes above.

Beyond types of app blocking functions, you can also choose what you see when you try to enter a blocked app or website. You can make a custom message for yourself, a contact, or even an alternative app in place of the distracting app. 

-Squads feature: maybe you need a friend to help keep each other accountable, it lets you do that. You can even join an existing squad if you have an invite link. This is probably also good for parents who need their kids to be off their electronic devices before bedtime. 

All in all, this app deserves its hype and I’m shocked that it isn’t more mainstream. I can’t tell you how many times I had mindlessly clicked on my social media apps while studying and for the app to snap me right out of it. And when I get the app to let me take a break, it will make sure that the 30 mins I select actually stays as 30 minutes. Seriously, support the devs if you can!

reviews.title: The best at what it does.
reviews.text:
Jomo as an app by itself has dramatically curved my phone usage. So it works as intended when you set it up upon installation. Where it differs with the other applications in this space has to do with the level of control offered + their philosophy around screen time. As I also believe, not all screen time is bad screen time. 

Let’s go back now. To Covid, 2020, and just how weird everything was online then. I am not afraid to admit to having once had a double digit screen time habit each day. This habit was ripping me apart to my core. It was but a symptom of a huge problem of myself being mindful and present. I think I may be speaking on behalf of others as well. 

I abruptly deleted my Facebook account during the Summer of 2023 as I could no longer take the pull of it and just how awful it was. Jomo had showed up on an ad somewhere in a social media feed. I had been using another famous app in this space on a yearly subscription. I was kind of disappointed with it however, due to the lack of control within the app and not much flexibility. Off the initial install, Jomo surprised me with its control and flexible approach towards using your phone. For instance, yes, I do want to block a lot of different apps that sink your time. But sometimes, I want to be intentional in that doom scroll. Jomo let’s you scale your block sessions in a way where you can finely tune your breaks down to the nearest 5 minute intervals or an hour. It uses a built in feature that lets you even express why you’re taking a break. This is extremely helpful and forms a sort of agreement to not stay too long out of the present moment. 

The above is but a small glimpse into what I like about this application. The developers are also great. Responsive and kind. Open to ideas as well and very innovative for such a small team. I went in on a lifetime membership for the above features and Team behind this application. Give it a try. Get off the Hedonic treadmill of dopamine addiction. Be intentional with the computer in your pocket :)
